parameters.note: Tahoe-tributary check (required for Tahoe-basin waters): the Rubicon River is NOT a Lake Tahoe tributary. It is a major tributary of the Middle Fork American River, with headwaters near Clyde Lake in the Crystal Range (Desolation Wilderness) that flow west/northwest away from Lake Tahoe. The represented reach is the upper river in Rockbound Valley (El Dorado Co.). Because the river drains to the American River rather than into Lake Tahoe, the §7.50(b)(152) 'Tahoe Lake tributaries' special closure does NOT apply. The Rubicon River is also not listed by its own name in §7.40(b) or §7.50(b), so it falls under the general statewide stream regulation §5.85(a)(2): open with a five-trout bag from the last Saturday in April through November 15, then a zero-trout catch-and-release period with gear restrictions from November 16 through the Friday preceding the last Saturday in April.

parameters.description: The represented upper-river reach in Rockbound Valley lies within the Desolation Wilderness (Eldorado National Forest / Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit; confirmed inside the Desolation Wilderness protected-area boundary). A wilderness permit is required to enter this reach: a free day-use permit (self-issued at major trailheads, no fee and not quota-limited) and, for overnight trips, an overnight permit required year-round; overnight use is governed by a zone-quota system in effect from the Friday before Memorial Day through September 30 each year, with permits and reservations handled through Recreation.gov (permit #233261). Note: the Rubicon River is ~60 miles long; its lower reaches (below the wilderness, toward Hell Hole Reservoir and the Middle Fork American River) are outside Desolation Wilderness and are not subject to this wilderness-permit requirement.
